title: Bench - PostgreSQL (Aurora, RDS Proxy)
description: Aurora writer and RDS Proxy (CloudWatch, 1 point per minute), engine statistics and statements (postgres_exporter, every 15 s).

panels.title: Capacity (ACU)
panels.description: Serverless v2: 1 ACU is about 2 GiB of memory with the matching CPU, by steps of 0.5. Empty with provisioned instances

panels.title: Capacity vs completed tasks
panels.description: How fast the capacity follows a burst, and how far it falls after it (the buffer pool with it)

panels.title: ACU utilization
panels.description: Capacity used over max_capacity: near 100 % the instance is capped, the scaling cannot help

panels.title: Freeable memory
panels.description: Grows and shrinks with the ACUs on serverless

panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio
panels.description: Drops after a scale-down: the pages of tasks and results come back from the storage

panels.title: CPU utilization
panels.description: On serverless, a share of the current capacity: high CPU at low ACU only means a scale-up is due

panels.title: Database load (average active sessions)
panels.description: Performance Insights in CloudWatch. Above the vCPUs: sessions queue for the CPU. Waits: locks, I/O, commits (details by wait event in the Performance Insights console)

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Every connection of the writer: RDS Proxy, the GetEvents streams, the monitoring

panels.title: Commit latency
panels.description: Aurora commits on 4 of 6 copies of the storage, in 3 zones

panels.title: Billed I/O per 5 min
panels.description: Billed per million on Standard storage, free on I/O-Optimized: Standard is cheaper while the I/O stay under about a quarter of the bill. Points every 5 minutes

panels.title: WAL generated and kept for replication
panels.description: The logical replication slots of GetEvents: a growing lag keeps WAL on the volume

panels.title: Client and server connections
panels.description: Borrowed at the max: the clients queue for a server connection (borrow latency). Max follows max_connections, which serverless derives from max_capacity

panels.title: Pinned server connections
panels.description: Pinned: a server connection kept by one client until it disconnects (prepared statements, SET, advisory locks), no longer shared. Must stay near 0, or the proxy is no pooler

panels.title: Borrow latency
panels.description: Time a client waits for a server connection of the pool

panels.title: Query latency through the proxy
panels.description: Proxy response minus database response: what the proxy adds to a query

panels.title: Logical replication slot lag (WAL broadcaster)
panels.description: WAL written but not yet confirmed by the WAL broadcaster of Core: must stay flat

panels.title: Connections by application and state
panels.description: Seen from the writer: the clients of the proxy show as the proxy's server connections

panels.title: Connections waiting, by wait event type

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (queryid) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total[$__range]))) * on (queryid) group_left (query) max by (queryid, query) (pg_stat_statements_query_id)

panels.title: Top statements: time per second

targets.expr: topk(8, sum by (queryid) (rate(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total[1m]))) * on (queryid) group_left (query) max by (queryid, query) (pg_stat_statements_query_id)

panels.description: Seconds of execution per second: the share of the database each statement takes

targets.expr: topk(8, sum by (queryid) (rate(pg_stat_statements_calls_total[1m]))) * on (queryid) group_left (query) max by (queryid, query) (pg_stat_statements_query_id)
